title: The Algebraic Reals are an Explicit Fσ — Completing the Gδ/Fσ Dichotomy
description: Dualizes the parent's dense-Gδ transcendentals to the algebraic side: the algebraic reals {x : ℝ | IsAlgebraic ℚ x} are exhibited as an explicit Fσ — the countable union ⋃_{a algebraic} {a} of closed singletons. Since Mathlib has the predicate IsGδ but no Fσ counterpart, this entry introduces IsFσ (a countable union of closed sets) and proves the De Morgan duality isFσ_iff_isGδ_compl: s is Fσ iff sᶜ is Gδ. It then derives the abstract lemma that every countable set in a T1 space is Fσ (dual to the parent's isGδ_compl_of_countable), applies it to the algebraic reals, and shows the transcendentals are NOT an Fσ (their Fσ-ness would make the algebraic reals Gδ, contradicting the parent). The headline is the packaged four-way classification: algebraic reals are Fσ-but-not-Gδ (and meagre), transcendentals are Gδ-but-not-Fσ (and comeagre) — the exact algebraic/transcendental analogue of ℚ/irrationals.

overview.historicalContext: The Fσ/Gδ distinction originates with René Baire and the early-20th-century descriptive set theory of Baire, Borel, and Lebesgue, who organized the pointclasses of the Borel hierarchy (Σ⁰₂ = Fσ, Π⁰₂ = Gδ). The canonical example is the rationals ℚ: they form an Fσ (a countable union of closed singletons) but, by the Baire Category Theorem, are not a Gδ — and dually the irrationals are a dense Gδ but not an Fσ. The algebraic/transcendental partition of ℝ is the exact analogue: the algebraic reals are countable (Cantor, 1874), hence meagre, and the transcendentals are comeagre and uncountable (Liouville's 1844 construction gave the first explicit transcendentals; Hermite 1873 and Lindemann 1882 settled e and π). The parent entry formalized the Baire-category half and the Gδ side; this entry supplies the dual Fσ side. Standard references are Oxtoby's Measure and Category (GTM 2) and Kechris's Classical Descriptive Set Theory (GTM 156).
overview.problemStatement: Mathlib carries the predicate $\mathrm{IsG\delta}$ (a countable intersection of open sets) but has no $F\sigma$ counterpart. The parent entry exhibits the transcendental reals $\{x : \mathbb{R} \mid \neg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\ \mathbb{Q}\ x\}$ as an explicit dense $G\delta$ and proves the algebraic reals $\{x : \mathbb{R} \mid \mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\ \mathbb{Q}\ x\}$ are not a $G\delta$. Its first open question asks for the dual: present the algebraic reals as an explicit $F\sigma$ — a countable union of closed singletons $\bigcup_{a\ \text{algebraic}} \{a\}$ — and record the full $G\delta/F\sigma$ classification of the dichotomy. Formally: define $\mathrm{IsF\sigma}$, prove the De Morgan duality $\mathrm{IsF\sigma}\ s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{IsG\delta}\ s^c$, show the algebraic reals are $F\sigma$, show the transcendentals are not $F\sigma$, and package the four-way classification.
overview.proofStrategy: First introduce IsFσ s as ∃ T : Set (Set X), (∀ t ∈ T, IsClosed t) ∧ T.Countable ∧ s = ⋃₀ T — a countable union of closed sets, dual to Mathlib's IsGδ. Prove both directions of the duality isFσ_iff_isGδ_compl: IsFσ.isGδ_compl complements a countable union of closed sets into a countable intersection of open sets via Set.compl_sUnion, and isFσ_of_isGδ_compl runs the reverse passage through compl_compl and Set.compl_sInter. Next prove isFσ_of_countable: in any T1 space a countable set s equals ⋃₀ ((fun a => {a}) '' s), each singleton closed by isClosed_singleton (T1), the index family countable by Set.Countable.image, simplified with Set.sUnion_image and Set.biUnion_of_singleton. Apply this to the algebraic reals, which are countable (AlgebraicNumbersCountable.algebraic_reals_countable), yielding algebraicReals_isFσ. For transcendentalReals_not_isFσ, assume they are Fσ; then by IsFσ.isGδ_compl their complement, the algebraic reals, would be a Gδ, contradicting the parent's algebraicReals_not_isGδ. Finally package algebraic_gδ_fσ_dichotomy from these facts plus the parent's transcendentalReals_isGδ.
keyInsights: Mathlib has IsGδ but no Fσ predicate, so the Fσ notion must be introduced locally; once defined as a countable union of closed sets, all Fσ results reduce to Gδ results under De Morgan complementation rather than requiring fresh topology.

The single lemma isFσ_iff_isGδ_compl (s is Fσ iff sᶜ is Gδ) is the workhorse: it transports every Gδ fact about complements into an Fσ fact, and is reusable for any descriptive-complexity argument over Mathlib.

Countability is the engine of the Fσ side: in a T1 space any countable set is automatically Fσ, since it is literally the countable union of its closed singletons {a} — no analytic input is needed beyond closedness of points.

The algebraic reals being Fσ-but-not-Gδ is forced by two independent facts working together: countability gives Fσ for free, while the parent's Baire-category argument (meagre + dense ⇒ not Gδ) rules out Gδ.

The transcendentals' failure to be Fσ is purely a duality consequence, not a separate proof: an Fσ transcendental set would make its algebraic complement a Gδ, directly contradicting the parent — so the negative result costs only one De Morgan step.

The completed picture is symmetric on two axes — Baire category (algebraic meagre / transcendental comeagre) and Borel complexity (algebraic Fσ-not-Gδ / transcendental Gδ-not-Fσ) — making the algebraic/transcendental partition an exact transported copy of ℚ versus the irrationals.

conclusion.summary: A 154-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization that completes the Gδ/Fσ classification of the algebraic/transcendental dichotomy. It introduces the Fσ predicate missing from Mathlib, proves its De Morgan duality with IsGδ, and uses it to exhibit the algebraic reals as an explicit Fσ (the countable union of closed singletons) while showing the transcendentals are not an Fσ.
conclusion.implications: The pairing is now symmetric on both axes: in Baire category the algebraic reals are meagre and the transcendentals comeagre (parent); in Borel complexity the algebraic reals are Fσ-but-not-Gδ and the transcendentals are Gδ-but-not-Fσ (here). This is precisely the structure of ℚ versus the irrationals, transported to the algebraic/transcendental partition. The locally-defined IsFσ predicate and the duality isFσ_iff_isGδ_compl are reusable for any descriptive-complexity argument over Mathlib, which currently lacks an Fσ notion.
openQuestions: Lift the Fσ/Gδ classification into Mathlib's Borel hierarchy: show the algebraic reals lie in Σ⁰₂ \ Π⁰₂ and the transcendentals in Π⁰₂ \ Σ⁰₂, connecting IsFσ/IsGδ to MeasurableSpace.GenerateMeasurable levels.
Make the Fσ presentation fully constructive by exhibiting an explicit enumeration a : ℕ → ℝ of the algebraic reals and the resulting increasing sequence of finite closed sets ⋃_{k ≤ n} {a k}.
